arguments.name: Abductive case for a nonphenomenal account
premises: Apparent phenomenality motivates explanation; realists and illusionists dispute what this appearance warrants.
Fallible representation could in principle generate phenomenal judgments without their proposed qualitative referents.
If a sufficiently adequate nonphenomenal account is available, theoretical economy can favor it.
bridge_principles: B-P2T05-01: Explanatory economy tracks the relevant truth only given adequate coverage and no stronger independently justified target datum.
B-P2T05-02: Psychological/representational explanation can capture the relevant epistemic achievement, not merely duplicate an utterance.
arguments.conclusion: Frankish infers that phenomenal realism is mistaken and favors illusionism; his practical recommendation is to develop the programme. This attribution does not establish the abductive premises or their truth-conduciveness.
arguments.strongest_objection: A-P2T05-002 disputes that the target is exhausted by fallible representations and asks whether the economy argument starts from a distorted target.
arguments.strongest_reply: A-P2T05-003 contests whether ostension fixes the target’s realist nature and returns the burden to an account of unmediated awareness.
unresolved_issues: No numerical abduction or metaphysical posterior.
Physicalism and causal closure are not empirically verified by this philosophical exchange.
CL-P2T05-013 causal correction and CL-P2T05-015 alternative concession must constrain reconstruction.

arguments.name: Experiential target, reference and immediate awareness
premises: Phenomenal consciousness concerns subjects undergoing experiential properties; an event-property description may distort the target.
Examples can establish reference without making their nature depend on a philosophical description.
On her account, undergoing an experiential property is already awareness of it; no additional representation is needed.
At least one relevant experiential example is actually instantiated.
bridge_principles: B-P2T05-03: The ostensively fixed experiential target includes the relevant what-it-is-like aspect without a theory-laden phenomenal-property premise.
B-P2T05-04: Immediate awareness is identical with experiential instantiation in the relevant sense and cannot be simulated by a merely functional seeming.
arguments.conclusion: Given the stated exemplification and target premises, denial of experiential consciousness fails; the argument is conditional, as her§4 explicitly says.
arguments.strongest_objection: A-P2T05-003 accepts the examples and commonality but disputes that they rule out a nonphenomenal interpretation; rejecting PPP alone cannot block a recast illusionist claim.
arguments.strongest_reply: Her§2 p7 supplies the immediate-awareness argument, and§3 p9 distinguishes misdescribing a real property from denying its instantiation. These address more than a bare assertion that consciousness exists.
unresolved_issues: This paper’s short explanations do not inspect its cited fuller2016a/2016b accounts.
The premise identifying awareness with instantiation cannot be certified by the author’s conviction.
Opposition does not contradict the attribution records.

arguments.name: Reply: reference need not settle nature
arguments.position: Frankish’s actual response to the selected critic
premises: Grant the subject-property recasting for argument.
Accept ordinary examples and a shared feature while interpreting that feature through representational states and dispositions.
Ostension need not guarantee the descriptive or metaphysical nature attributed to its target.
bridge_principles: B-P2T05-05: The proposed nonphenomenal interpretation is a live explanation of the very target introduced, rather than a substitute phenomenon.
B-P2T05-06: Cognitive access to structural/dispositional physical properties requires mediation; direct acquaintance cannot independently settle the question.
arguments.conclusion: Reference fixing alone does not rule out his illusionist ontology; the remaining immediate-awareness disagreement reaches explicitly acknowledged metaphysical commitments.
arguments.strongest_objection: Nida-Rümelin’s positive awareness premise targets B-P2T05-05/06: preserving verbal examples need not preserve the experiential property she points to.
arguments.strongest_reply: He does not merely deny the examples: he specifies an alternative account of their commonality. His physicalist refusal of robust acquaintance is candidly qualified as unpersuasive to this critic.
unresolved_issues: The reply does not supply a neutral proof that Nida-Rümelin’s target is entirely captured.
Physicalist motivation is not an independently established premise.
No subsequent Nida-Rümelin response was required or established by these searches.

arguments.name: Illusion, regress and the remaining content burden
arguments.position: Strong sourced challenge and the selected author’s replies
premises: If the supposed illusion itself has phenomenal character, phenomenality has not been eliminated.
If it is only a coarse belief, the account may fail to explain experiential richness.
If each apparent feel requires a higher phenomenal representation, the explanation risks regress or a concealed phenomenal starting point.
bridge_principles: B-P2T05-07: An illusion of phenomenality needs the relevant phenomenal seeming; this must be argued, not assumed from the everyday word illusion.
B-P2T05-08: The offered nonphenomenal representations can explain content, richness and reactions without a conscious internal audience.
arguments.conclusion: The regress objection identifies a real explanatory constraint; it is not automatically a contradiction once functional seeming and limited introspection are allowed.
arguments.strongest_objection: Merely renaming a state a nonphenomenal representation does not explain why it presents determinate apparent qualities or captures what the critic means by experience.
arguments.strongest_reply: Original§§3.2–3.4 rejects phenomenal content vehicles and inner observers; reply pp9–10 allows a limited higher-order route; p23 allows fine-grained nonphenomenal states. None is claimed as a completed mechanism.
unresolved_issues: Nida-Rümelin notes and sets aside the short illusion-presupposes-consciousness line; this map does not falsely attribute a developed regress proof to her.
The Prinz/Pereboom alternatives are seen through Frankish’s reply; their originals remain uninspected.
A modal prohibition on functional seeming and an adequate worked model remain distinct unresolved demands.
